stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: The generator forces a sinusoidal EMF $u(t) = U_\text{max}\cos(\omega t)$ on the series RLC circuit. Sweep the pulsation $\omega$ and the resistance $R$ — watch $i(t)$: the peak swells as $\omega$ approaches the resonance value $\omega_0 = 1/\sqrt{L\,C}$. Move BOTH sliders AND cross through resonance to advance.
stages.concept: In steady state $i(t) = I_\text{max}\cos(\omega t - \varphi)$ with $I_\text{max} = U_\text{max}/Z$ and $Z = \sqrt{R^{2} + (L\omega - 1/(C\omega))^{2}}$. Amplitude peaks when the reactive part vanishes: $L\omega_0 = 1/(C\omega_0)\ \Rightarrow\ \omega_0 = 1/\sqrt{L\,C}$, where $Z = R$ and $I_\text{max} = U_\text{max}/R$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Hit the target amplitude marker $I^{*}$ on the chart — tune $\omega$ and $R$ so your peak current matches within $\pm 5\%$. Many $(\omega, R)$ pairs work: only the impedance $Z$ matters here.
stages.concept: $I^{*} = U_\text{max}/Z^{*}\ \Rightarrow\ Z^{*} = U_\text{max}/I^{*}$. Pick any $(\omega, R)$ with $\sqrt{R^{2} + (L\omega - 1/(C\omega))^{2}} = Z^{*}$. Fastest route: at $\omega = \omega_0$ the reactance vanishes, so $R = Z^{*}$.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: Only the target sinusoid is drawn. Read its period $T$ from the peak-to-peak spacing, compute $\omega^{*} = 2\pi/T$, set the $\omega$ slider, then press RUN to overlay your curve. Match $\omega$ to within $\pm 3\%$.
stages.concept: The forced current has the same period as the drive: $T = 2\pi/\omega$. Read $T$ from two consecutive peaks of the target curve, invert to get $\omega^{*}$. $R$ shifts the amplitude but does not change the period.

labels.peek_hint: read the period T between two peaks on the target — ω = 2·π / T
labels.tip1: sweep ω across its range; watch the peak grow near ω₀ = 1/√(L·C)
labels.tip2: tune ω and R so the peak of your curve touches the orange I* line
labels.tip3: read the target's period, compute ω, then press RUN

1.1: Slide ω slowly from small to large. The peak of i(t) grows, maxes out, then shrinks again.
1.2: The maximum occurs at ω₀ = 1/√(L·C). With L = 1 H and C = 1 mF, ω₀ ≈ 31.6 rad/s.
1.3: At resonance, Z reduces to R. Smaller R gives a taller peak — try R at its minimum and sweep ω through resonance.

2.1: Compute Z* = U_max / I*. Then any (ω, R) whose impedance equals Z* hits the target.
2.2: Set ω = ω₀ so the reactance is zero — then R alone controls I_max. Adjust R until R = Z*.
2.3: If I* is large (≥ 200 mA), you need a small R near resonance. If I* is small (< 100 mA), move ω far from ω₀.

3.1: Look at the target sinusoid: measure the horizontal distance between two consecutive peaks — that is the period T.
3.2: Invert: ω* = 2π / T. Set the ω slider to that value; ignore R for now (only ω is judged).
3.3: R does not change the period, only the peak height. The reveal shows amplitude mismatch but tolerance is on ω.
